title: Component inputs
summary: Pass data from a parent component into a child with the input() function.

docs.title: Angular: Accepting data with input properties

quiz.q: What does a child component use to receive data from its parent?
quiz.explain: `input()` declares a value the parent can set from its template. `output()` is for the opposite direction.

quiz.q: Make `name` a required input of type string.
quiz.explain: `input.required<string>()` means the parent must supply the value, or the build reports an error.

quiz.q: A child has `score = input(0);` and the parent writes `<app-badge />` without a score. What does `{{ score() }}` show?
quiz.explain: The number in `input(0)` is the default used when the parent gives nothing.

quiz.q: Click the line with the mistake. The child declares `name = input.required<string>();`.
quiz.explain: An input is a signal, so it must be read with parentheses: `{{ name() }}`.

quiz.q: Which parent template passes the number 82 to the input `score`?
quiz.explain: `[score]="82"` binds the number 82. Plain `score="82"` would pass the text '82', which is a string.

exercise.task:
Finish `badge.component.ts`.

- Import `input` from `@angular/core`.
- In `StudentBadgeComponent` create `name = input.required<string>()` and `score = input(0)`.
- Its template shows `{{ name() }}` and `{{ score() }}`.
- In `AppComponent` add `imports: [StudentBadgeComponent]`.
- In the parent template use `<app-student-badge name="Asha" [score]="82" />`.
hints: Inputs are class fields created by calling `input...()`. Read them in the template with parentheses.
A component placed in another template must be listed in that component's `imports`. Use `[score]` to pass a number.

checks.name: name is a required string input
score is an input with default 0
The child template reads name() and score()
checks.hint: Use {{ name() }} and {{ score() }} with parentheses.
